concepts.name: Shared Responsibility Model
concepts.what: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud; you are responsible for security IN the cloud.
concepts.use: Any question asking who patches, secures, encrypts, configures, or controls access.
facts: AWS: data centers, hardware, networking foundation, hypervisor, managed-service infrastructure.
Customer: data, IAM, encryption choices, network rules, app code, EC2 guest OS.
EC2: you patch OS. RDS/DynamoDB/Lambda: AWS manages much more infrastructure.
traps: Do not assign IAM, data classification, security groups, or app security to AWS.
Do not say AWS patches the guest OS on your EC2 instances.

concepts.name: IAM And Roles
concepts.what: IAM controls who can do what. Roles provide temporary credentials and are best for AWS services.
concepts.use: EC2/Lambda needs access to S3/DynamoDB, least privilege, MFA, root user protection.
facts: Use IAM roles for AWS services; avoid access keys on EC2.
Use least privilege policies.
Enable MFA, especially for root and privileged identities.
IAM is global.
traps: IAM user keys are long-term credentials and should not be hardcoded.
Cognito is for application users; IAM Identity Center is workforce SSO.

concepts.name: CloudTrail vs CloudWatch vs Config
concepts.what: Three services often appear together: API audit, monitoring, and configuration compliance.
concepts.use: Audit, alarms, metrics, logs, compliance, or configuration history questions.
facts: CloudTrail = who did what API action and when.
CloudWatch = metrics, logs, dashboards, alarms.
AWS Config = resource configuration history and compliance rules.
traps: CloudWatch does not show who made API calls.
CloudTrail does not monitor CPU performance.
Config records/evaluates configuration; it is not primarily a threat detector.

concepts.name: Security Services
concepts.what: Match the security service to the threat or compliance need.
concepts.use: Threat detection, vulnerability scanning, PII discovery, DDoS, web attacks, reports.
facts: GuardDuty = managed threat detection.
Inspector = vulnerability scanning for EC2/ECR/Lambda workloads.
Macie = sensitive data discovery in S3.
WAF = SQL injection and XSS web rules.
Shield = DDoS protection.
Artifact = compliance reports and agreements.
traps: Do not choose GuardDuty for vulnerability scanning; that is Inspector.
Do not choose Macie unless the question says sensitive data/PII in S3.

concepts.name: EC2 Pricing
concepts.what: Choose the EC2 purchase option from duration, predictability, and interruption tolerance.
concepts.use: Most cost-effective EC2 questions.
facts: On-Demand = short-term, unpredictable, no commitment, cannot be interrupted.
Reserved Instances = steady 1-year/3-year instance usage.
Savings Plans = flexible compute spend commitment for EC2, Fargate, Lambda.
Spot = interruptible, fault-tolerant, batch, simulation, CI jobs.
Dedicated Host = physical host for licensing/compliance.
traps: Spot is wrong for uninterruptible workloads.
Reserved is usually wrong for only a few weeks/months.
Capacity Reservation reserves capacity but does not create a discount by itself.

concepts.name: Billing Tools
concepts.what: Billing tools split into estimate, analyze, alert, detailed report, and rightsize.
concepts.use: Cost visibility, forecast, budgets, TCO, or optimization questions.
facts: Pricing Calculator = estimate before deployment.
Cost Explorer = visualize historical and forecasted cost/usage.
AWS Budgets = alerts and budget reports.
Cost and Usage Report = detailed raw billing data.
Compute Optimizer = rightsizing recommendations.
Migration Evaluator = migration business case/TCO.
traps: Pricing Calculator is before deployment; Cost Explorer is after usage exists.
Budgets alerts; it is not the main visualization tool.

concepts.name: Support Plans
concepts.what: Support questions ask about response times, Trusted Advisor, technical support, and TAMs.
concepts.use: TAM, 24/7 support, business-critical release, Trusted Advisor full checks.
facts: Basic is included and covers account/billing resources plus core support resources.
Business/Business Support+ is for production support and 24/7 expert access.
Enterprise Support includes designated TAM and production-critical response up to 15 minutes.
Developer Support, Business Support, and Enterprise On-Ramp are scheduled for discontinuation on January 1, 2027 outside GovCloud; exams may still use legacy names.
traps: A dedicated TAM is Enterprise, not Basic or Developer.
For strategic planning and event support during a critical release, choose Enterprise Support.

concepts.name: S3 And Storage Classes
concepts.what: S3 is object storage. Storage classes are mostly about access frequency and retrieval time.
concepts.use: Object storage, static websites, data lakes, archive, accidental deletion, lifecycle.
facts: S3 Standard = frequent access.
Standard-IA = infrequent access across multiple AZs.
One Zone-IA = cheaper, one AZ, re-creatable data.
Intelligent-Tiering = unknown or changing access patterns.
Glacier Instant = archive with millisecond retrieval.
Glacier Flexible/Deep Archive = low-cost archive with slower retrieval.
Versioning protects from accidental overwrite/delete.
traps: S3 is not block storage; EBS is.
Lifecycle moves/deletes automatically; replication copies objects.

concepts.name: EBS vs EFS vs FSx vs Instance Store
concepts.what: These are common storage traps around block, file, and temporary storage.
concepts.use: Storage attached to EC2, shared file system, Windows file shares, HPC, ephemeral disk.
facts: EBS = block storage for EC2, AZ-scoped, persistent.
EFS = shared Linux NFS file system, multi-AZ.
FSx = managed file systems such as Windows File Server and Lustre.
Instance Store = temporary local disk lost on stop/terminate.
Storage Gateway = on-premises access to cloud storage.
traps: Do not choose EBS when many instances need a shared Linux file system; choose EFS.
Do not choose Instance Store for persistent data.

concepts.name: Compute Chooser
concepts.what: Compute questions are usually about control level and operational overhead.
concepts.use: Servers, serverless code, containers, app deployment, batch jobs.
facts: EC2 = virtual machines and OS control.
Lambda = run code without servers for event-driven tasks.
Fargate = serverless containers.
ECS = AWS-native container orchestration.
EKS = managed Kubernetes.
Elastic Beanstalk = upload app code and AWS provisions platform resources.
Batch = batch processing jobs.
App Runner = containerized web app from source/image with low overhead.
traps: Lambda has execution limits and is not a regular long-running server.
Fargate still runs containers; it just removes EC2 management.

concepts.name: Database Chooser
concepts.what: Pick database services by data model and workload pattern.
concepts.use: Relational, NoSQL, graph, warehouse, cache, document database, SQL on S3.
facts: RDS = managed relational databases.
Aurora = AWS cloud-native MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible relational database.
DynamoDB = serverless NoSQL key-value/document.
Redshift = data warehouse/OLAP analytics.
Athena = serverless SQL queries over S3 data.
Neptune = graph relationships/fraud.
ElastiCache/MemoryDB = Redis/in-memory caching.
DocumentDB = MongoDB-compatible document database.
traps: Redshift is not OLTP app database.
Athena does not store data; it queries S3.
DynamoDB is not relational SQL.

concepts.name: Networking Chooser
concepts.what: Network questions are mostly about routing, private access, acceleration, and hybrid connectivity.
concepts.use: DNS, CDN, global low latency, private subnet outbound, dedicated connection, private service access.
facts: VPC = isolated virtual network.
Route 53 = DNS and domain routing.
CloudFront = CDN content caching at edge.
Global Accelerator = improves app traffic over AWS global network.
Internet Gateway = public internet for VPC.
NAT Gateway = private subnet outbound internet.
Direct Connect = dedicated private connection.
Site-to-Site VPN = encrypted internet tunnel.
PrivateLink = private access to supported services without public internet.
traps: CloudFront caches; Global Accelerator does not cache.
Direct Connect is dedicated but slower to provision; VPN is faster to set up.

concepts.name: Security Groups vs NACLs
concepts.what: Security Groups are stateful resource firewalls; NACLs are stateless subnet firewalls.
concepts.use: Allow ports, deny IPs, subnet-level firewall, instance-level firewall.
facts: Security Groups operate at ENI/resource level and are stateful.
NACLs operate at subnet level and are stateless.
Security Groups allow rules only; NACLs can allow and deny.
traps: For explicit deny at subnet level, choose NACL.
For allowing a port to EC2, Security Group is usually the answer.

concepts.name: High Availability And Reliability
concepts.what: Availability keeps systems running; reliability recovers from failure and meets demand.
concepts.use: Multi-AZ, disaster recovery, auto recovery, load balancing, no single point of failure.
facts: Use multiple AZs for high availability inside a Region.
Use multiple Regions for disaster recovery/geographic isolation.
Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic.
Auto Scaling adds/replaces EC2 capacity.
RDS Multi-AZ is failover; read replicas scale reads.
traps: Read replica is not the same as Multi-AZ failover.
Edge locations are not AZs or Regions.

concepts.name: Well-Architected Framework
concepts.what: AWS best-practice framework with six pillars.
concepts.use: Any question asking which pillar or design principle.
facts: Pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.
Reliability = recover from failures and meet demand.
Performance Efficiency = right resource types and efficient use.
Cost Optimization = avoid unnecessary cost.
Operational Excellence = run and improve systems.
traps: High availability, scalability, and durability are not pillar names.
For “recover automatically from service interruptions,” choose Reliability.

concepts.name: AWS CAF
concepts.what: Cloud Adoption Framework organizes cloud transformation into business and technical perspectives.
concepts.use: CAF perspective and cloud transformation questions.
facts: Perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations.
Business = strategy and value.
People = culture, skills, cloud fluency.
Governance = risk, portfolio, cloud financial management.
Platform = technical foundation.
Operations = run, monitor, improve.
traps: Sustainability and Reliability are Well-Architected pillars, not CAF perspectives.
Cloud fluency belongs to People.

concepts.name: Migration And Hybrid
concepts.what: Migration questions ask whether you are discovering, moving apps, moving databases, transferring files, or staying hybrid.
concepts.use: On-premises migration, disconnected sites, hybrid compliance, database migration.
facts: Application Discovery Service = collect on-prem usage/configuration.
Application Migration Service = lift-and-shift servers.
DMS = database migration; SCT = schema conversion.
DataSync = online data movement.
Transfer Family = SFTP/FTPS/FTP to S3/EFS.
Snow Family = offline transfer or disconnected edge processing.
Outposts = AWS infrastructure on-premises.
traps: DMS migrates databases, not EC2 servers.
Snowball Edge is good when network is limited or local processing is needed.

concepts.name: Integration Services
concepts.what: Integration services decouple and coordinate applications.
concepts.use: Queue, fanout notification, workflow, event bus, contact center, email.
facts: SQS = queue and decouple producers/consumers.
SNS = pub/sub push notifications, fanout, SMS/email.
EventBridge = event bus and SaaS/AWS events.
Step Functions = workflow orchestration.
SES = email sending.
Amazon Connect = cloud contact center.
traps: SNS pushes; SQS stores messages for polling.
Step Functions coordinates steps; it is not a queue.

concepts.name: Analytics And AI
concepts.what: For CLF-C02, match the service to the use case, not implementation detail.
concepts.use: ETL, dashboards, streaming, search, ML, NLP, image recognition.
facts: Glue = ETL and data catalog.
QuickSight = BI dashboards.
Kinesis = real-time streaming data.
OpenSearch = search/log analytics.
SageMaker = build/train/deploy ML.
Rekognition = image/video.
Comprehend = natural language.
Lex = chatbot.
Polly = text-to-speech.
Transcribe = speech-to-text.
Textract = extract forms/tables text.
Kendra = intelligent enterprise search.
traps: QuickSight visualizes; Athena queries.
Kinesis streams; SQS queues.

concepts.name: Cloud Value And Exam Words
concepts.what: Many questions test AWS value proposition and key words.
concepts.use: Agility, elasticity, scalability, economies of scale, global reach, variable expense.
facts: Agility = quickly provision and experiment.
Elasticity = acquire/release resources as demand changes.
Scalability = handle growth.
Economies of scale = lower variable costs from AWS scale.
Trade fixed for variable expense = pay as you go instead of buying data centers.
Go global in minutes = deploy near users through Regions and edge network.
traps: Elasticity is demand-based resource adjustment, not simply high availability.
Eliminating all operational work is usually too absolute.

questions.q: A company plans to use an Amazon Snowball Edge device to transfer files to the AWS Cloud. Which activities related to a Snowball Edge device are available to the company at no cost?
opts: Use of the Snowball Edge appliance for a 10-day period
The transfer of data out of Amazon S3 and to the Snowball Edge appliance
The transfer of data from the Snowball Edge appliance into Amazon S3
Daily use of the Snowball Edge appliance after 10 days
questions.explain: Data transfer FROM Snowball Edge INTO S3 is free. The appliance rental costs apply after the free period. Data transfer OUT of S3 to Snowball incurs charges.

questions.q: A company has deployed applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to assess application vulnerabilities and must identify infrastructure deployments that do not meet best practices. Which AWS service can the company use?
questions.explain: Amazon Inspector automatically assesses applications for vulnerabilities and deviations from best practices. Trusted Advisor gives recommendations. Config tracks config changes. GuardDuty detects threats.

questions.q: A company has a centralized group of users with large file storage requirements. The company wants to extend file storage while retaining performance benefits of sharing content locally. What is the MOST operationally efficient AWS solution?
opts: Create an S3 bucket for each user
Configure and deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway
questions.explain: Storage Gateway File Gateway provides on-premises access to cloud storage using standard file protocols (NFS/SMB), caching frequently accessed data locally.

questions.q: According to security best practices, how should an Amazon EC2 instance be given access to an Amazon S3 bucket?
opts: Store keys in text file on EC2
Have EC2 assume an IAM role
Modify S3 bucket policy to allow any service
questions.explain: IAM Roles provide temporary, automatically rotated credentials. Never hardcode credentials or store them in files. Follow least privilege.

questions.q: Which option is a customer responsibility when using Amazon DynamoDB under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?
opts: Encryption of data at rest in DynamoDB
questions.explain: Customer manages access to DynamoDB tables via IAM policies. AWS handles physical security, patching, and infrastructure.

questions.q: Which option is a perspective that includes foundational capabilities of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?
questions.explain: AWS CAF has 6 perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations. Governance includes portfolio management, risk management.

questions.q: A company is running and managing its own Docker environment on EC2. The company wants an alternative to help manage cluster size, scheduling, and environment maintenance. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explain: AWS Fargate is serverless compute for containers, eliminating EC2 instance management for container workloads.

questions.q: A company wants to run a NoSQL database on Amazon EC2 instances. Which task is the responsibility of AWS in this scenario?
questions.explain: For EC2 (IaaS), AWS manages physical infrastructure, hardware, and hypervisor. Customer manages guest OS, DB, and security groups.

questions.q: Which AWS services or tools can identify rightsizing opportunities for EC2 instances? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: Cost Explorer and Compute Optimizer provide rightsizing recommendations based on usage patterns and CloudWatch metrics.

questions.q: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Trusted Advisor? (Choose two.)
opts: Detecting underutilized resources to save costs
questions.explain: Trusted Advisor provides real-time guidance in 5 categories: cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, service limits.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage that users experience when they move on-premises workloads to AWS?
opts: Elimination of expenses for running and maintaining data centers
Identical price discounts to hardware providers
Distribution of all operational controls to AWS
questions.explain: AWS eliminates the need to run and maintain physical data centers, shifting to pay-as-you-go model.

questions.q: A company wants to manage deployed IT services and govern its infrastructure as code (IaC) templates. Which AWS service?
questions.explain: Service Catalog allows organizations to create and manage catalogs of approved IT services and IaC templates.

questions.q: Which AWS service helps users visualize, understand, and manage spending and usage over time?
questions.explain: Cost Explorer visualizes, analyzes, and forecasts costs and usage over time.

questions.q: A company uses a central data platform to manage multiple data types. The company wants to discover, transform, and visualize data. Which combination? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: AWS Glue for ETL (extract, transform, load) and QuickSight for data visualization and BI dashboards.

questions.q: A global company wants to migrate third-party apps to AWS with help from a global team of experts following AWS best practices. Which AWS service?
questions.explain: AWS Professional Services provides global teams of experts to help with migration and implementation.

questions.q: An e-learning platform runs an app for 2 months/year. Any downtime must be avoided. Which EC2 option is MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: For short, predictable bursts (2 months) without interruption tolerance, On-Demand is most cost-effective vs long-term commitments.

questions.q: A developer wants to deploy an application quickly without manually creating resources. Which AWS service?
questions.explain: Elastic Beanstalk is PaaS that automatically handles deployment, capacity provisioning, load balancing, and scaling.

questions.q: A company stores sensitive data in S3 and wants to protect against accidental deletion or overwriting. Which S3 feature?
questions.explain: S3 Versioning keeps multiple versions of objects, protecting against accidental deletion or overwrites.

questions.q: Which AWS service provides the ability to manage infrastructure as code?
questions.explain: CloudFormation uses templates (JSON/YAML) to provision and manage AWS resources as code.

questions.q: An online gaming company needs EC2 instances for 1 year. Traffic is consistent and predictable. Instances must be online without disruption. MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: Reserved Instances offer up to 72% discount for steady, predictable workloads with 1 or 3-year commitment.

questions.q: Which AWS service allows a user to establish a dedicated network connection between on-premises data center and AWS?
questions.explain: Direct Connect provides dedicated private physical connections with consistent low latency and high bandwidth.

questions.q: Which option is a physical location of the AWS global infrastructure?
questions.explain: AWS Regions are physical geographic locations with multiple Availability Zones.

questions.q: A company wants to protect AWS Cloud information while performing risk assessment and mitigation. Which Well-Architected pillar?
questions.explain: The Security pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets through risk assessment and mitigation.

questions.q: What is the purpose of having an internet gateway within a VPC?
opts: Allow communication between VPC and internet
questions.explain: Internet Gateway (IGW) enables communication between instances in the VPC and the internet.

questions.q: A monolithic on-premises app is migrating to AWS as microservices. Which Well-Architected best practice?
questions.explain: Loosely coupled dependencies allow components to fail independently, supporting microservices architecture.

questions.q: A company wants to audit password and access key rotation details for compliance. Which AWS service?
questions.explain: IAM credential reports provide details on user credentials status, including password and access key rotation.

questions.q: A company wants notification when a specific AWS cost threshold is reached. Which services? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: AWS Budgets and CloudWatch can both trigger notifications when cost thresholds are exceeded.

questions.q: Which AWS service provides answers to frequently asked security-related questions from users?
questions.explain: AWS Knowledge Center provides answers to common security and service-related questions.

questions.q: Which tasks are customer responsibilities under Shared Responsibility Model? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: Customers configure security groups and classify assets. AWS manages DynamoDB patching and infrastructure.

questions.q: Which are pillars of AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: The 6 pillars are: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.

questions.q: Which AWS service sends both text and email messages from distributed applications?
questions.explain: Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service) sends messages via SMS, email, and other protocols to distributed apps.

questions.q: A user needs programmatic access to AWS through CLI or API. Which option?
questions.explain: Access keys (Access Key ID and Secret Access Key) enable programmatic access via CLI and SDKs.

questions.q: A company runs thousands of stateless, fault-tolerant simulations using AWS Batch (up to 3 hours each). MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: Spot Instances offer up to 90% savings for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads that can tolerate interruptions.

questions.q: What does agility mean in AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: Agility refers to speed of implementing resources and ability to experiment quickly with minimal effort.

questions.q: A company needs to block SQL injection attacks. Which AWS service?
questions.explain: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) blocks common web exploits like SQL injection and XSS.

questions.q: Which AWS service identifies if S3 bucket or IAM role has been shared with external entity?
questions.explain: IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources shared with external entities outside your AWS account.

questions.q: A cloud practitioner needs AWS compliance reports before migration. How to generate them?
questions.explain: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO) and agreements.

questions.q: An ecommerce company migrated from on-premises to AWS. Which cost is company's direct responsibility?
opts: Cost of hardware infrastructure on AWS
Cost of power for AWS servers
Cost of physical security for AWS data centers
questions.explain: Customer is responsible for their own software licenses. AWS manages hardware, power, and physical security.

questions.q: A company sets up IAM. Which recommendation complies with IAM best practices?
opts: Turn on MFA for added security
questions.explain: Enabling MFA adds an extra security layer. Never use root keys, don't grant broad permissions, always rotate credentials.

questions.q: Elasticity in AWS Cloud refers to: (Choose two.)
opts: Ease of procuring resources when needed
questions.explain: Elasticity means right-sizing resources as demand shifts and easily procuring/releasing resources as needed.

questions.q: Which service enables customers to audit API calls in their AWS accounts?
questions.explain: CloudTrail records API activity (who, what, when, from where) for auditing and compliance.

questions.q: What is customer responsibility when using AWS Lambda under Shared Responsibility Model?
questions.explain: For Lambda (serverless), customer manages only the code. AWS handles all infrastructure, OS, and scaling.

questions.q: A company has 5 TB in S3 and wants to occasionally query data for analysis. MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: Amazon Athena allows serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data. Pay only per query, no infrastructure needed.

questions.q: Which AWS service can be used at no additional cost?
questions.explain: AWS Organizations is free. You only pay for AWS resources created within accounts. Other services have usage costs.

questions.q: Which AWS CAF capability belongs to the people perspective?
questions.explain: Cloud fluency is a People perspective capability, focusing on workforce skills and digital readiness.

questions.q: A company wants upfront commitment for continued EC2 use in exchange for reduced cost. LOWEST cost? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans offer the lowest costs for steady, predictable workloads with commitments.

questions.q: A company wants to migrate on-premises relational DBs to AWS near current location. Which service/region?
questions.explain: AWS Regions allow deploying resources in specific geographic areas close to current locations.

questions.q: A company exploring AWS needs to create cost estimates before provisioning. Which service?
questions.explain: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs for AWS services before deployment.

questions.q: A company builds an app delivering images/videos globally with minimal latency. MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: CloudFront caches content at Edge Locations globally, reducing latency and being cost-effective for global delivery.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of economies of scale in cloud computing?
opts: Lower variable costs over fixed costs
questions.explain: Economies of scale mean AWS reduces costs over time due to massive scale, passing savings to customers.

questions.q: Which is a software development framework to define cloud resources as code via CloudFormation?
questions.explain: AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit) lets you define infrastructure using familiar programming languages.

questions.q: An app uses multiple AWS services and needs temporary, limited-privilege credentials for authentication. Which service?
questions.explain: AWS STS (Security Token Service) provides temporary, limited-privilege credentials for authentication.

questions.q: Which AWS service is a CSPM service aggregating alerts from AWS and partners in standardized format?
questions.explain: Security Hub aggregates and normalizes security findings from multiple AWS services and partners.

questions.q: Which AWS service is always provided at no charge?
questions.explain: IAM is free. You only pay for other AWS resources created. IAM itself has no charge.

questions.q: To reduce costs, a company migrates NoSQL DB to AWS. Which fully managed service auto-scales throughput?
questions.explain: DynamoDB is serverless NoSQL with automatic throughput scaling and single-digit millisecond latency.

questions.q: A company uses DynamoDB. Which task is company's responsibility under Shared Responsibility Model?
questions.explain: Customer manages access permissions via IAM. AWS handles OS, infrastructure, and patching for DynamoDB.

questions.q: A company testing an app can tolerate interruptions and doesn't need continuous run. MOST cost-effective EC2?
questions.explain: Spot Instances are ideal for interruptible workloads, offering up to 90% discount.

questions.q: Which AWS service gives ability to discover and protect sensitive data in S3?
questions.explain: Macie uses ML to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data in S3.

questions.q: Which can block network traffic to an instance? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: Security Groups (instance level) and NACLs (subnet level) control inbound/outbound network traffic.

questions.q: Which AWS service can identify when an EC2 instance was terminated?
questions.explain: CloudTrail logs all API calls, including instance termination events with details of who, when, and from where.

questions.q: Which is a fully managed MySQL-compatible database?
questions.explain: Aurora is MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible, offering 5x MySQL performance with full managed service benefits.

questions.q: Which AWS service supports hybrid architecture extending AWS infrastructure to on-premises data centers?
questions.explain: AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure, services, and APIs to on-premises facilities.

questions.q: Which AWS service runs managed PostgreSQL database providing OLTP?
questions.explain: Amazon RDS manages relational databases including PostgreSQL for OLTP workloads.

questions.q: A company wants managed Windows virtual desktops and applications for remote employees. (Choose two.)
questions.explain: WorkSpaces provides managed virtual desktops. AppStream 2.0 streams desktop applications to browsers.

questions.q: A company wants to monitor for misconfigured security groups allowing unrestricted access. Which service?
questions.explain: Trusted Advisor includes security checks that flag open security groups (e.g., 0.0.0.0/0 on specific ports).

questions.q: Which AWS service is a key-value database providing sub-millisecond latency at scale?
questions.explain: DynamoDB is a fully managed key-value and document database with single-digit millisecond latency.

questions.q: A company deploying ML project needs compute power over several months. Jobs don't need specific times. LOWEST cost?
questions.explain: Spot Instances are ideal for flexible, non-time-critical workloads, offering up to 90% savings.

questions.q: Which provide disaster recovery solutions for EC2? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: AMIs capture instance configurations. EBS snapshots capture volume data. Both enable recovery and replication.

questions.q: Which AWS service provides command line access to AWS tools directly from a web browser?
questions.explain: CloudShell provides browser-based, pre-authenticated shell access with AWS CLI pre-installed.

questions.q: A network engineer builds hybrid cloud with Direct Connect. Expects hundreds of VPCs. Which service to simplify connectivity?
questions.explain: Transit Gateway acts as a cloud router, simplifying connectivity between multiple VPCs and on-premises networks.

questions.q: A company wants to assess operational readiness and mitigate risks ahead of product launch. Which Support plan?
questions.explain: Enterprise Support includes Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) for event readiness at no additional charge.

questions.q: A company wants to schedule rotation of database credentials with LEAST operational overhead. Which service?
questions.explain: Secrets Manager automatically rotates, manages, and retrieves database credentials with minimal overhead.

questions.q: Which can create a private connection between on-premises and AWS workloads?
questions.explain: Direct Connect establishes dedicated private network connections from on-premises to AWS.

questions.q: Which AWS service provides encryption for Amazon EBS?
questions.explain: AWS KMS (Key Management Service) manages encryption keys for EBS volumes and other services.

questions.q: A company wants to manage AWS Cloud resources through a web interface. Which service?
questions.explain: AWS Management Console is the web-based interface for managing AWS services visually.

questions.q: Which are advantages of AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: AWS offers economies of scale and global reach in minutes. Capital expenses become variable, not vice versa.

questions.q: Which AWS Cloud benefit shows architecture's ability to withstand failures with minimal downtime?
questions.explain: High Availability (HA) ensures systems remain operational with minimal downtime despite failures.

questions.q: A developer needs repeatable dev and prod infrastructure. Which service?
questions.explain: CloudFormation enables repeatable infrastructure deployment via templates (IaC).

questions.q: Which is customer responsibility under Shared Responsibility Model?
questions.explain: Customers configure firewalls (security groups, NACLs). AWS maintains infrastructure security and patches RDS.

questions.q: Which AWS service delivers highly available applications with fast failover for multi-Region/Multi-AZ?
questions.explain: Global Accelerator improves availability and performance with fast failover across Regions using AWS global network.

questions.q: Ecommerce apps need to send messages to each other. Which service?
questions.explain: SQS decouples application components by storing messages in queues for asynchronous processing.

questions.q: Benefits of consolidated billing? (Choose two.)
questions.explain: Consolidated billing combines usage for volume discounts and provides a single bill across all accounts.

questions.q: A user wants to review all S3 buckets with ACLs and policies. Which service?
questions.explain: Access Analyzer for S3 reviews bucket policies and ACLs to identify public or shared buckets.

questions.q: Best resource for compliance-related information and reports about AWS?
questions.explain: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO) and agreements.
